claim: MemOS leads the eligible original HaluMem QA panel on accuracy, benchmark-labeled hallucination and omission in both lengths.
source_locations: halumem.pdf pp. 10–11, §4 and Table 3; Appendix B.1 pp. 18–19; title and MemOS reference, pp. 1 and 15
mathematical_result: Medium 67.23% / 15.17% / 17.59%; Long 64.44% / 16.61% / 18.95%. Hallucination 4.00 and 0.68 pp lower than Mem0 respectively. Nine joint dominance edges persist at 0–5 pp.
verification_status: Verified within protocol; retrieval cap attribution corrected
limitations: Developer-linked panel; seven authors also appear on cited MemOS paper. GPT-4o generator and judge. Hallucination includes incorrect and fabricated answers. Same user histories, method-specific APIs and budgets. Memobase has 500-token cap and Long nonclosure. No paired intervals.

claim: MemOS has weak distractor resistance and the Long update metrics expose omission trade-offs.
mathematical_result: MemOS false-memory resistance 44.94% Medium / 28.85% Long. Long update hallucination 0.29% vs Mem0 0.03%; omission 34.47% vs 98.51%.
limitations: Extraction and update implementations and output profiles differ. False-memory resistance is a distractor diagnostic; it is not an open-answer rate.

claim: SIRIN Judge faithfulness-only lowers strict unfaithfulness among served answers while reducing coverage.
source_locations: sirin.pdf p. 11, Table 8 and accompanying text
mathematical_result: Mem0 35.1%→23.2% (−11.9 pp); LightMem 33.1%→22.1% (−11.0 pp); both 100%→80% coverage. Mem0 Judge answerability-only 40.9%.
limitations: Shared questions, retrospective transductive thresholds, a GPT-5.4-mini gate and independent Claude Sonnet 5 strict-label judge. Aggregate coverage products require aligned weighting/inclusion. No verified empirical all-query effect or CI for unfaithfulness.

claim: SIRIN Judge both-gates raises served accuracy relative to each ungated base.
source_locations: sirin.pdf p. 11 Table 8 caption and p. 6 Table 5 for the separate SimpleMem scope
mathematical_result: Mem0 +13.2 pp, 95% CI [10.1,16.4]; LightMem +14.3 pp, [11.0,17.7]; coverage 62.0% and 63.6% respectively.
verification_status: Verified as published paired cluster-bootstrap result
limitations: Intervals concern served accuracy. SimpleMem Table 5 has a different filter and the strict endpoint uses the probe training label. Neither interval compares memory frameworks.

claim: TRUSTMEM has lower reported consolidation transition error than the matched-backbone Mem-T anchor.
source_locations: trustmem.pdf p. 3 Figure 2 and pp. 8–10 §§4.1, 4.5; p. 15 Table 6; p. 17 Appendix D
mathematical_result: Hallucination 0.01% vs 0.05% (−0.04 pp); omission 8.08% vs 13.48%; corruption 0.14% vs 2.21%.
limitations: GPT-4o-mini (temperature zero) labels major errors on transitions from 463 validation instances. Method-specific transition counts, paired intervals and a common denominator of user outcomes are unavailable. Caption's 50% uses AtomMem (0.02%) as lowest nominal baseline, a different backbone. No confirmed matched downstream hallucination benefit.

claim: RootMem adds local implicit-logic benefits to three base systems on the IMLogic MCQ protocol.
mathematical_result: MemOS 39.44→51.04%, LightMem 37.55→50.23%, EverMemOS 43.50→50.41%. All three dominate their own bases through 5 pp on the joint objective set.
limitations: Forced-choice trap choices are diagnostic. Table 5 shares an answerer, memory model and top-30 budget. No reported paired uncertainty. IMLogic reuses HaluMem-Medium user histories and contributes no independent external replication.

claim: BioMem HMRU-R improves updating while HMRU-T weakens selected QA outcomes.
source_locations: biomem.pdf p. 14 Table 4, p. 16 Figure 7 and §2.3.4
mathematical_result: HMRU-R updating QA +3.03 pp vs A-Mem (tie at 5 pp). HMRU-T updating and temporal QA −12.12 and −25.00 pp; temporal recall +12.50 pp. Figure 7 reports 26 fixed and 10 broken, exact two-sided McNemar p=0.01133 from these discordances.
verification_status: Verified within one medical cohort; auxiliary p-value verified
limitations: Frozen reader and medical subset; Table 4 QA and Fig. 7 perfect answers are distinct endpoints. No question-cluster uncertainty recoverable from discordant totals. HMRU-R proactive-alignment QA −0.81 pp.

claim: RMM improves LongMemEval QA within each named retriever comparison.
source_locations: rmm.pdf p. 7 Table 1 and preceding experimental setup
mathematical_result: GTE 63.6%→70.4%, +6.8 pp; +10.69% relative accuracy, +18.68% relative judged-error reduction. Contriever +2.4 pp; Stella +3.4 pp.
limitations: Retrieval/reranking and context construction differ despite shared retriever names. Means over three runs with no reported paired dispersion. Error complement is not a direct hallucination measure.

claim: MemGPT improves historical fact retrieval versus lossy-summary controls under three reader backbones.
source_locations: memgpt.pdf p. 5 Table 2 and §3.1.1; p. 11 Appendix §6.1
mathematical_result: Accuracy gains +28.2, +60.4, +58.1 pp; ROUGE-L recall gains +0.235, +0.518, +0.468. Three joint edges robust across tolerance grid.
limitations: Summary-only controls abstain when information is insufficient, while MemGPT is instructed to guess using paginated full-history access. Three backbones reuse one workload; no paired uncertainty. Reference-based scores are memory-performance proxies.

claim: Original LongMemEval-M supports narrower retrieval and QA comparisons.
source_locations: longmemeval.pdf pp. 9–10 Tables 3–4; derived head-to-head protocol filters
mathematical_result: Session QA .670→.714 with fact augmentation; temporal Recall@5 .639→.722 and NDCG@5 .630→.732 with fact keys plus GPT-4o query expansion.
limitations: These are controlled scores for retrieval/QA, not direct hallucination. Tables share original-question lineage and provide no paired intervals.

claim: Agreement across weighting schemes gives no evidence of equal architectural performance.
mathematical_result: 1,605/1,605 profiles have one matched endpoint, one protocol and one cohort. All four weightings coincide.
limitations: A singleton eliminates numerical weighting leverage by construction. Counts do not imply independent evidence.

claim: No identifiable pooled global ranking or general-purpose shortlist is supported.
source_locations: data/comparability.csv; data/comparison_blocks.csv; Stage 2B compatibility audit; RootMem p. 3; HaluMem p. 8
mathematical_result: 4,370 eligible contrasts, 140 blocks and 28 recorded cohort labels; 0 aligned pooled cross-cohort matches in 713 baseline-relative scopes.
limitations: Projection edges conflate concrete configurations and heterogeneous endpoints. Shared histories and baselines induce dependence, including IMLogic–HaluMem, SIRIN–LongMemEval, and medical RealMem–full RealMem. No common outcome model or aligned external replication is established.
